hints.content: Note that the graph of $g$ can be obtained by transforming the graph of $f$, since $g(x)=f(x+3)$. [[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Given that $f(x)=-\dfrac{1}{4}x^2$, we have the following:

>$\begin{align}f(x)&=-\dfrac{1}{4}x^2\\\\
f(x+3)&=-\dfrac{1}{4}(x+3)^2\\\\
\end{align}$

Notice that what is on the right-hand side of the equal sign is $g(x)$.  Therefore, $g(x)=f(x+3)$.

hints.content:
Replacing $x$ with $x+3$ shifts the graph of $f$ to the left by $3$ units.

Therefore, *the graph of $g$ is obtained by shifting the graph of $f$ to the left by $3$ units.*
